_comment: Feature 058 / item #184 — the measured incident, frozen.
This is the fast-uri case as it stood on main before feature 057 remediated it, and it is the
acceptance test for #184: a lockfile pinned BELOW a fix that the existing override range ALREADY
PERMITS. If a change does not clear this, it does not address the incident.
lockfile    fast-uri@3.1.4                   <- pinned the vulnerable one
advisory    GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7  published 2026-08-03   (THREE DAYS AFTER the fix)
outcome     sast gate red for TEN DAYS, and a four-week acceptance written
Renovate proposed nothing and structurally could not: `>=3.1.4 <4` satisfies every 3.x, so there
was no range to widen, and it reasons about the manifest range rather than the lockfile.
FROZEN DELIBERATELY. The live cases this feature also clears (hono, undici 6.x) are remediated by
058's own follow-up PR, so a test relying on them would stop failing for the right reason. This
file keeps the incident reproducible after the repository has moved on.
The extra rows are the boundary cases that must NOT produce refresh advice: a resolution outside
the override's range, a fix beyond the override's ceiling, an already-remediated pin, and a
package with no override at all.

findings.title: fast-uri bypasses the previous fix (the incident)
fix lies beyond the override's exclusive upper bound — floor must be raised
resolution outside the override's range — the override cannot reach it
resolution inside the override's range and below the fix — refresh clears it
resolved version already at or above the fix floor
package carries no override at all
